verdict.rationale: Activepieces ships a built-in MCP server that external clients such as Claude, Cursor and Codex can connect to. It lets them build and test flows, and the embeddable MCP gives a backend a token to run a user's automations through AI. That covers calling workflows from an external agent. The evidence does not show individual connected-app actions, or specific chosen flows, being published as discrete callable MCP tools; the documented server is mainly platform-management oriented. missing for 10: documented per-flow or per-piece-action exposure as named MCP tools, tool schema/selection controls for what is exposed, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can expose my workflows or connected app actions as MCP tools that an external agent can call

citations.quote: Activepieces includes a built-in MCP server that lets AI assistants build flows, manage tables, test automations, and more
Connect Claude, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client and it drives the whole platform.
your backend gets a token it can use to run that user's automations through AI.
